d.d: To incite or cause troublesome acts; to encourage; to instigate.
d.x: He was arrested for fomenting a riot; after all, it's bad enough being in a riot but starting one is much worse.

d.d: To apply a poultice to; to bathe with a cloth or sponge.
simple past and past participle of foment
present participle and gerund of foment
To experience FOMO (“the fear of missing out”); to act on one's FOMO, often impulsively [(often) with into].
